subject: Re: [AMBER] {SPAM?} Re: Raw RDF exceeds total number of waters?

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
Hi,
Sorry for the delay on this. The answer is pretty straightforward
actually - the "raw" RDF is literally that - just the total bin
counts, so if you're doing more than one frame you'll easily get more
than the total number of waters in the system. Try it on a single
frame to see what I mean. Hope this helps,
-Dan
On Thu, Sep 8, 2022 at 4:02 PM Matthew Guberman-Pfeffer
<matthew.guberman-pfeffer.uconn.
edu> wrote:
>
> Hi Dan,
>
> I mean that the number of waters+Na+ is 59559, and the raw RDF quickly exceeds 100,000.
>
> Best,
> Matthew
>
>

org> wrote:

> > amber.ambermd.org> wrote:
> >
> >> Dear Amber Community,
> >>
> >> The below CPPTRAJ command gives me raw RDF values that exceed the number
> >> of waters in the simulation box:
> >>
> >> radial out rdf.dat 0.1 15 :WAT,Na+ :1280 density 0.033456 intrdf
> >> intrdf.dat rawrdf rawrdf.dat bymol1
> >>
> >> Is it an imaging issue?
> >>
> >> What I’m really concerned about is the same command run on two different
> >> trajectories with identical counts of WAT and Na+ gives me raw RDF values
> >> that almost systematically differ by a factor of ~2. The only difference
> >> between the simulations is the temperature. I need to know if the
> >> difference is real.
> >>
> >> Best,
> >> Matthew
